assumptions: Arrival context not specified by the orchestrator; read as Daniel arriving from a Google search for 'milestone birthday' while planning his partner's 40th alongside the wedding.
HTML comments, image slot notes and fact markers treated as invisible.

Business details (fees, commissions, on-the-ground support, transfers, room blocks, Wedded Privileges, phone lines) are deliberately deferred per the orchestrator, so their absence is noted but not scored as a draft failure and no edits are suggested to add them.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic, finance background)
Every suggested edit 'old' is an exact unique substring of 05-draft.md
No suggested edit adds prices, fees, commissions, vendor names, statistics words or em dashes, or asks how the fee is worked out

open_questions.question: Daniel's enquiry score is held down mainly by deferred business detail (what the service includes and how pricing works). Confirm the panel should treat this as out of scope for this post rather than a draft fault.

first_impression.reaction: Intro is plain and gets on with it. No 'unforgettable' or 'magical'. I jumped to the FAQ first like I always do, it was sensible but generic, so I went back and skimmed the rest. The actual sources on candles, sun and travel insurance are what kept me in.

journey.quote: Neither is better. A party gathers everyone in one room, while a trip gives a smaller group real time together. Some hosts do both.
journey.reaction: Good. Nobody is trying to push me to the expensive option. That's the first thing I check.

journey.quote: As a suggestion, start several months ahead for a weekend away.
journey.reaction: 'Several months' is vague, but at least it's honest that it's a suggestion and not a made-up rule. I'd rather that than a fake number.

journey.quote: as the [SA Metropolitan Fire Service candle fact sheet](https://www.mfs.sa.gov.au/community-safety/safety-and-education/fact-sheets/candles2/mfs-fact-sheet-candles.pdf) sets out.
journey.reaction: Linked source from an actual fire service. This is the kind of thing that tells me someone checked rather than wrote from vibes.

journey.section: A long lunch or garden party
journey.quote: In Australia, sun protection is recommended whenever UV levels reach 3 or higher, and UV cannot be seen or felt, so check the UV for your location before the day
journey.reaction: Concrete threshold, cited to Cancer Council. Practical for a Brisbane lunch.

journey.section: A party at home or a destination weekend
journey.quote: | Hosting load | Concentrated on one day | Spread over several days, with more to organise ahead |
journey.reaction: A trade-off table that actually lists the downside of the destination option. That's the honest framing I want.

journey.section: Choose the date and book the anchor event
journey.quote: What will you confirm in writing, and when?
journey.reaction: Best line in the piece for me. Questions to put to a venue in writing is exactly how I'd protect myself after last time.

journey.quote: Declare everything upfront, including pre-existing health conditions, or the policy may be void.
journey.reaction: Useful, specific, sourced to Smartraveller. Honest about where things go wrong.

journey.section: Where everyone stays and one hosted dinner
journey.quote: Wedded Concierge plans milestone birthdays through the same Wedded Advisor process: one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as a single point of contact, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: Sales pitch dropped in the middle of the travel advice. And 'couples' in a birthday article reads like it was pasted from a wedding page. Makes me wonder what else is boilerplate.

journey.section: Celebrating a milestone as a couple
journey.quote: A joint celebration halves the travel for guests and doubles the reason to come.
journey.reaction: Cute line, but it's not literally true. 'Halves the travel' is a claim I'd pick at. Just say guests travel once.

journey.section: Planning a milestone birthday with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: A milestone birthday brings people together from near and far, and it deserves the care of any celebration that does.
journey.reaction: Filler. Tells me nothing. This is where I want the facts, not a greeting card.

journey.section: Planning a milestone birthday with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins
journey.reaction: That's a real commitment and the most reassuring sentence about the service. Fee in writing up front means fewer surprises.

journey.section: Planning a milestone birthday with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, anywhere in the world
journey.reaction: 'Anywhere in the world' is a big claim with nothing next to it. Show me one real example and I'd believe it.

unanswered_questions: Is there a real milestone birthday this team has planned that I can look at, even a short write-up?
What does 'anywhere in the world' mean in practice: any country, or the destinations on the site?
Does the Wedded Advisor also cover a party at home in Australia, or only travel celebrations?
If we're already planning a wedding with Wedded Concierge, can a birthday weekend be added to the same advisor?

turn_offs_found.quote: Wedded Concierge plans milestone birthdays through the same Wedded Advisor process: one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as a single point of contact, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD for Australian couples.
turn_offs_found.why: CTA before any evidence the service has done birthdays, and 'couples' signals copy reused from a wedding page.

turn_offs_found.quote: A milestone birthday brings people together from near and far, and it deserves the care of any celebration that does.
turn_offs_found.why: Emotional padding exactly where I want facts about the service.

turn_offs_found.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, anywhere in the world
turn_offs_found.why: Sweeping claim with no example or proof alongside it.

would_share_with: My partner, for the venue questions list and the travel insurance checklist

cta_reaction.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, anywhere in the world, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
cta_reaction.why: The fee-in-writing line is the only thing pulling me towards it. The advice is good and honest, but the page gives me no proof the service has done this before, so I'd bookmark it and look up reviews first.

top_3_changes: Fix 'quoting in AUD for Australian couples' to 'clients' so the birthday pitch doesn't read as pasted from a wedding page.
Replace the empty opener of the closing section with a plain line saying what you're handing over, so the facts come first.
Swap 'halves the travel ... doubles the reason to come' for a literal statement; overclaims, even playful ones, make me doubt the rest.

suggested_edits.old: quoting in AUD for Australian couples
suggested_edits.new: quoting in AUD for Australian clients
suggested_edits.reason: This is a birthday article. 'Couples' reads as copy reused from a wedding page and makes a sceptical reader wonder what else is boilerplate.

suggested_edits.old: A milestone birthday brings people together from near and far, and it deserves the care of any celebration that does.
suggested_edits.new: If you would rather not run the planning yourself, this is what handing it over looks like.
suggested_edits.reason: Removes emotional filler at the point where a sceptical reader wants plain facts, and leads straight into the service description.

suggested_edits.old: A joint celebration halves the travel for guests and doubles the reason to come.
suggested_edits.new: A joint celebration means guests make one trip instead of two, with two reasons to come.
suggested_edits.reason: 'Halves the travel' is a loose quantitative claim. Saying it literally keeps the same point without an overclaim.

suggested_edits.old: A long weekend with close friends at a villa or a small hotel: one anchor dinner, a long lunch, and the rest left open. The pace is the point.
suggested_edits.new: A long weekend with close friends at a villa or a small hotel: one anchor dinner, a long lunch, and the rest left open so guests can set their own pace.
suggested_edits.reason: 'The pace is the point' is a slogan. The rewrite says the same thing as a practical reason.
